compensating.why: hop 1 counts the year of era, not the proleptic year, from 1900
hop 2 takes the month from the start of the date in Joda-Time's default zone
hop 3 takes the day of month from the start of the date in Joda-Time's default zone

ownership_reason: Only the gold searches for the start of the day: hops 1-3 gather the receiver's year, month and day of month in the form the JDK uses and hop 4 passes them on, so no caller holds an instant before the gold returns, and no choice of fields naming the same day moves the gold's search, which starts 24 hours before the JDK's noon of that day. Once the gold has returned its Date, the start of the day can come back only if a caller searches again from the gold's result, a second implementation of the gold's search. The gold's javadoc promises a Date at the start of the day in the default time zone of the JDK; on the trigger the variant returns 03:00 on a day that starts at 02:40. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the facade's own javadoc ('The time will be set to the earliest valid time for that date'); LocalDateTime.toDate, the sibling conversion, sets the earliest valid time after a gap by stepping forward by minutes and back by seconds (TestLocalDateTime_Basics testToDate_springDST_2Hour40Savings, same zone, expects 02:40, passes); DateTimeZone.getOffsetFromLocal moves a local time in a gap to after the gap (TestDateTimeZoneCutover test_getOffsetFromLocal_NewYork_Spring); LocalDate.toDateTimeAtStartOfDay converts to the earliest valid time for the date (testToDateTimeAtStartOfDay_avoidDST); TestLocalDate_Basics testToDate_springDST pins the start of a day without midnight on the facade's own path.
